title: Daily Variance Sprint Map — Jamal Reyes
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Short running scratchpad to track day-to-day variance vs my personal sprint commitments (2-week cadence). Treat as both a lightweight diary and an experiment log.
- Goal: surface small mismatches early so I can run micro-experiments instead of big last-minute patches.

How I use this doc (operational):
- Every morning: 2 minute scan, set a single guardrail for the day ("no new deep design tasks", "block time for 2x OKR touch-ups").
- End of day: quick 3-line capture: plan -> actual -> micro-adj.
- Weekly: synthesize 5 days into a single retrospective + 1 experiment to run next week.

Current 2-week sprint (2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-14):
- Northstar/OKR focus: Increase feature rollout observability (Personal OKR: OWN-1)
  - Key result A: Ship rollout telemetry dashboard for 2 routes (target: 95% coverage).
  - Key result B: Reduce average time-to-detect regressions from 48h to 12h.

Daily variance map (template):
- Date | Plan (1–2 bullets) | Actual (1–2 bullets) | Delta / why | Small countermeasure (1 action)

Entries (recent):
2026-03-10 | Finalize dashboard wireframe; review with Mira | Wireframe done; review postponed (blocked by infra data sampling question) | Blocked by infra sampling parity (mismatch between test and prod streams) | Ping Owen for quick data sample and add fallback mitigator (sample-stub)
2026-03-09 | Author collection spec for rollout events | Drafted spec but too long; missed clarity on edge-case enums | Over-optimizing schemas in the moment -> delayed | Trim to "must-have" fields; add a follow-up doc for enums
2026-03-08 | Run hourly ingestion smoke tests, validate metrics pipeline | Tests flaky; found two upstream lag spikes | Pipeline backpressure during GC windows; noise in staging | Add metric: ingestion-lag-95th to alerts; schedule tests offset from GC windows

Weekly retro notes (quick):
- Signal: I constantly over-index on "perfect schema" which reduces shipping cadence.
- Hypothesis: If I adopt a "schema v1 (minimal) + v2 follow-up" pattern, I can hit more incremental releases with fewer blockers.
- Experiment to run (this sprint): For any telemetry schema, only require 3 fields for v1 (id, timestamp, event_type). Track how many follow-ups needed.
- Dangerous assumption: that downstream consumers will tolerate schema changes; mitigation: add compatibility note and opt-out gate.

Micro-experiments & results log:
- Experiment: "3-field schema" (started 2026-03-02) -> result so far: shipped to staging without downstream breakage; 1 consumer asked for 1 extra field -> resolved via optional field. Signal: positive.
- Experiment: "Daily 10-min blocking review" (start 2026-02-22) -> result: reduced mid-week surprises but doubled interrupt context switches; refinement: move review to end-of-day for better flow.

Metrics I glance at (personal shortlist):
- Weekly deploys touching telemetry routes (target >= 3 per sprint)
- Mean time to detect anomaly (MTTD) for my routes
- Number of schema follow-ups created within 2 weeks of release (target <= 2)
- Days with uninterrupted 2-hour deep focus (target >= 3/week)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do I need to centralize sampling parity checks into a checklist with infra? (ticket?)
- What's an acceptable SLAT for rollout telemetry starting v1? (ask SRE and Mira)

Action backlog (top of mind):
- [ ] Create stub endpoint for sampling parity (owner: Owen) — due 2026-03-12
- [ ] Trim telemetry schema to minimal v1 and publish compatibility note — owner: Jamal — due 2026-03-11
- [ ] Draft RBAC note for dashboard view scopes and share with product ops — owner: Jamal — due 2026-03-14

Signals to watch next week:
- A spike in ingestion-lag-95th > 5s during business hours -> treat as P1 for the sprint
- More than 1 follow-up request per telemetry release -> trigger schema review ritual

Short retrospective voice memo (notes to self):
- Don't let 'perfect' be the enemy of 'observable'. Small, instrumented releases win.
- Prioritize blocking mitigations over speculative optimizations.

Reference links (quick):
- Confluence: rollout-telemetry-guidelines (link above)
- Slack: convo with Mira on "schema parity" (search: #mira-schema-parity)
- Local: /notes/temporal-sampling-checklist (personal folder)

Quick wins I can do this afternoon (under 30m):
- Add ingestion-lag-95th to this sprint's dashboard (5–10m)
- Convert schema doc to two pages: v1 required vs v2 optional (15–20m)

Notes-to-self tone: keep entries terse, timestamp everything, and err on the side of shipping small experiments. If this doc grows into operational ground truth, move to shared drive and create a proper PRD.
